title: Troubleshooting
blurb: Memory, disk, budgets, debate and MT-Bench.

blocks.html: Each model's serving settings live in slmjury/configs/models.yaml. Override them for your hardware without editing the file:
These change speed and memory use, not sampling, so the verdicts stay comparable. Lower --max-num-seqs first, then spread the model over more GPUs.

blocks.text: The disk fills up during a run

blocks.html: vLLM writes temporary files to /tmp. Point them at a larger disk, and start workers with spawn:

blocks.text: A judge never runs at 10 tokens

blocks.html: Judges marked always_thinks: true in models.yaml reason before every verdict and cannot answer in one word, so the runners skip the 10-token budget for them and run 8,192 only.

A debate keeps several agents' contexts in memory at once. slmjury/strategies/debate.py sets lower batch sizes for debate runs per model; lower them further for your GPUs, or run fewer configurations at a time with python scripts/run_debate.py --configs 0.

The reference scorers run through the Together API. Set TOGETHER_API_KEY, and install the extra with pip install "slmjury[together]". Each request is retried with a growing delay; the retry count, delays and timeout are set per scorer under reference_models in models.yaml.

blocks.text: MATH comparisons differ on another machine

blocks.html: MATH answers are compared with SymPy's LaTeX parser, which changes between versions. The package pins sympy==1.13.1 and antlr4-python3-runtime==4.11, and ships the decision for every MATH answer in the study in slmjury/parsers/math_labels.json, so the analyses read the shipped decision instead of parsing again.
Runners that take --force skip output files that already exist, so running the same command again does only the missing files. Pass --force to redo everything.
